Research Note · V1.0 · 2026-08-20

Energy-Efficient Multi-Hop Wireless Communication

Analytical and computational investigation of energy-optimal hop count in low-power wireless links

AUTHOR Sanjay Bhandari
STATUS Computational study complete
DOMAIN Wireless Networks · Low-Power Systems · Energy Optimization · Distributed Systems

Abstract

A controlled analytical and computational study of the trade-off between propagation-related transmit energy and per-hop circuit energy in multi-hop wireless communication.

Research Question

For a wireless communication path of fixed total distance, how does the number of relay hops affect the total energy required to successfully transmit a packet?

Analytical Model

E(H) = A/H + BH

The model represents total communication energy as the sum of a propagation-related component that decreases with hop count and a per-hop circuit component that increases with hop count.

Computational Experiments

  • Distance
  • Frequency
  • Receiver sensitivity
  • Circuit power
  • PA efficiency
  • Packet size
  • Data rate
  • Maximum TX power

Baseline Result

Optimal hop count 1
Minimum energy 2.178313e-05 J

Results

Limitations

  • Free-space propagation model
  • Equal hop lengths
  • Identical radios
  • Fixed circuit power
  • Fixed PA efficiency
  • Simplified packet-latency abstraction
  • No fading or shadowing
  • No interference model
  • No retransmission model
  • No MAC overhead
  • No mobility
